provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Letters Aa to Hh
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write capital and small letters Aa to Hh.
The pupils should be able to match capital letters to small letters.

Introduction:
Today we learn letters A to H.
We know some letters already.

Content:
Write big A and small a on the board.
Write big B and small b on the board.
Continue to H.
Point to each letter as we say its name.
Play a matching game with letter cards.

Class activity:
Each pupil writes Aa to Hh in their notebook.
Then they match capital to small letters on paper.

Evaluation questions:
What is the first letter?
Show me capital C.
What comes after D?

Summary:
We learned letters A to H today.
We can write them all.

topics.title: Letters Ii to Pp
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write capital and small letters Ii to Pp.
The pupils should be able to copy three rows of letters neatly.

Introduction:
We learned letters A to H last week.
Today we learn more letters.

Content:
Write big I and small i on the board.
Write big J and small j on the board.
Continue to P.
Show how to write each letter properly.
Demonstrate copying rows of letters.

Class activity:
Pupils write Ii to Pp in their notebooks.
They copy three rows of these letters.
Teacher helps those who need it.

Evaluation questions:
What is the middle letter?
Show me capital K.
How many letters do we write?

Summary:
We learned letters I to P today.
We can copy rows of letters.

topics.title: Letters Qq to Zz
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write the last letters Qq to Zz neatly.
The pupils should be able to say the whole alphabet in order.

Introduction:
We learned many letters already.
Today we finish the alphabet.

Content:
Write big Q and small q on the board.
Write big R and small r on the board.
Continue to Z.
Practice saying the whole alphabet.
Sing the alphabet song together.

Class activity:
Pupils write Qq to Zz in their notebooks.
Then they say the alphabet with the teacher.

Evaluation questions:
What is the last letter?
Sing the alphabet from A to Z.
Which letter comes after X?

Summary:
We learned all letters today.
We can say the whole alphabet.

topics.title: Numbers 1 to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write numbers 1 to 10 in order.
The pupils should be able to count as they write each number.

Introduction:
We know numbers from one to five.
Today we learn up to ten.

Content:
Write number 1 on the board.
Write number 2 on the board.
Continue to 10.
Show how to write each number properly.
Count objects as we write each number.

Class activity:
Pupils write numbers 1 to 10 in their notebooks.
They count aloud as they write each number.

Evaluation questions:
What number comes after five?
Show me number seven.
Count from one to ten.

Summary:
We learned numbers 1 to 10 today.
We can count as we write.

topics.title: Numbers 11 to 20
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write teen numbers.
The pupils should be able to trace the tens.

Introduction:
We know numbers up to ten.
Today we learn teen numbers.

Content:
Write number 11 on the board.
Write number 12 on the board.
Continue to 20.
Point to the tens place in each number.
Show how teen numbers are formed.

Class activity:
Pupils write numbers 11 to 20 in their notebooks.
They trace the tens place with colored pencils.

Evaluation questions:
What number comes after fifteen?
Show me number eighteen.
How many tens in number 20?

Summary:
We learned teen numbers today.
We can count to twenty.

topics.title: Two letter words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write two letter words.
The pupils should be able to read what they write.

Introduction:
We know our letters now.
Today we make words with two letters.

Content:
Write at on the board.
Write in on the board.
Write up on the board.
Write on on the board.
Read each word aloud with the pupils.

Class activity:
Pupils write at, in, up, on in their notebooks.
They read the words to their friend next to them.

Evaluation questions:
What word starts with a?
Show me the word in.
Can you read all the words?

Summary:
We learned two letter words today.
We can read what we write.

topics.title: Three letter words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write three letter words.
The pupils should be able to say the sounds as they write.

Introduction:
We made two letter words last week.
Today we make three letter words.

Content:
Write cat on the board.
Write dog on the board.
Write sun on the board.
Write cup on the board.
Say each sound as we write the word.

Class activity:
Pupils write cat, dog, sun, cup in their notebooks.
They say each sound as they write the letters.

Evaluation questions:
What word has the sound /k/?
Show me the word dog.
Can you make a new word?

Summary:
We learned three letter words today.
We can say the sounds as we write.

topics.title: My name and my class
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their full name by copying.
The pupils should be able to write their class.

Introduction:
Everyone has a special name.
Today we write our names and class.

Content:
Write your name on the board.
Write your class on the board.
Show how to write capital letters for names.
Show how to leave space between words.

Class activity:
Pupils copy their full name from the board.
They write their class name in their notebooks.

Evaluation questions:
What is your first name?
Can you write your full name?
What class are you in?

Summary:
We wrote our names today.
We know our class name.

topics.title: Neat pages
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write on the line and sit well.
The pupils should be able to hold the pencil right.

Introduction:
Good writing needs good posture.
Today we learn to write neatly.

Content:
Show how to sit straight on the chair.
Show how to hold the pencil properly.
Demonstrate writing on the line.
Explain why neat writing matters.

Class activity:
Pupils practice writing on lines in their notebooks.
Teacher checks how they hold their pencils.

Evaluation questions:
How should you sit when writing?
Show me how to hold a pencil.
Why do we write on the line?

Summary:
We learned to write neatly today.
Good writing needs good posture.

topics.title: Revision and writing show
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write their best handwriting.
The pupils should be able to write the alphabet from A to Z.

Introduction:
We learned many things this term.
Today we show our best writing.

Content:
Review all letters from A to Z.
Review all numbers from 1 to 20.
Review simple words we learned.
Show examples of good handwriting.

Class activity:
Pupils write their best page of handwriting.
They write the alphabet from A to Z.
Teacher displays best work on the wall.

Evaluation questions:
What is your favorite letter?
What is your favorite number?
Can you write your name?

Summary:
We showed our best writing today.
Everyone did a great job.
